mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic activity and increases S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when FEDFUNDS is low, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 7% signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when UNRATE drops below 7%, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and industrial production indicate strong demand, boosting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when both proxies rise, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising inflation (CPI) leads to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are positive when CPI rises in late-cycle, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when HOUST is high, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payroll signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when PAYEMS increases by 50k, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production and GDP indicate strong supply, boosting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when both proxies rise, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening cycle, rising FEDFUNDS increases borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are positive when FEDFUNDS rises in tightening cycle, or Rank IC < 0.03.
